summary: Bear River refuge Perry Entrance steel tower erected in 1934 and rebuilt in 1935 at the North End station; sources differ on how it ended, with a photo caption dated around 1990.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts lists it as removed and the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Tower Gone; WillhiteWeb captions describe it fallen around 1990. No removal date or cause agreed by the sources

access.note: Refuge open to visitors; auto tour route sunrise to sunset; no source describes the Perry Entrance site now

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1934 report places a tower at the Perry entrance; the 1935 entry moves a 40-foot Headquarters tower to the North End station, which Willhite identifies as the Perry Entrance. The sources do not say whether these are one tower or two, and the story says so.
Forest Lookouts lists it as removed; Willhite captions describe a fallen tower around 1990. Both agree it is gone, and the story reports both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Only the two Forest Lookouts pages, the WillhiteWeb page and the FFLA list cover this tower; none gives a removal date or cause, and no source ties it to the 1983 flood, so the story does not mention the flood. Two accounts conflict on the origin (a 1934 Perry tower versus a 1935 move to the North End station) and on the ending (removed versus fallen around 1990). The Perry coordinate 41.44799, -112.06786 comes from FFLA and is unchecked. A refuge Facebook post, seen only as a search snippet and not readable through fetch_text, may describe later towers and should be checked against these dates before publication; it was not used. No photo added.
